entities.summary: Amalric I of Jerusalem, king from 1163 to 1174, played a crucial role in shaping the history of the Crusader Kingdom. Born into the noble family of Lusignan, he ascended to the throne following the death of his father, Baldwin III, and ruled until his own death in 1174. His reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Fatimid Caliphate in Egypt and Syria, which ultimately led to the recapture of the city of Beirut. Despite his military successes, Amalric I's policies were also criticized for their harshness, particularly towards the local Christian population. The kingdom's economic situation during his reign was also precarious, with a significant decline in trade and a growing debt. Amalric I's legacy is complex and multifaceted, with some historians viewing him as a skilled military leader, while others see him as a ruthless and power-hungry ruler. He died in 1174, and his death marked the beginning of a period of instability in the kingdom, which would eventually lead to its downfall.
